Photoreductive 1,4-Dicarbofunctionalization of 1,3-Enynes with
Organoiodides and Cyanoarenes via Halogen-Atom Transfer

ABSTRACT: A photoreductive halogen-atom transfer (XAT) strategy for 1,4-dicarbofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes with
organoiodides and cyanoarenes is disclosed, enabling access to functionalized allenes in a highly regio-, chemo-, and stereoselective
manner. Upon the photoredox catalysis and the activation of Et
3
N XAT agents, the mild conditions and high functional group
tolerance of this protocol enable the formation of two C−C bonds, including a C(sp
3
)−C(sp
3
) bond and a C(sp
2
)−C(sp
2
) bond, in
a single reaction step, and provides a general avenue to polysubstituted allenes and late-stage modification of bioactive compounds.
A
llenes are valuable structural motifs frequently in natural
products, bioactive molecules, and functional materials, as
both end products and versatile building blocks.
1
For these
reasons, much sustained attention has been paid to the
development of efficient methodologies for building diverse
functionlized allene frameworks.
2
Among them, the 1,3-enyne
difunctionalization reaction has proven uniquely powerful to
staightfoward access of allenes using readily accessible starting
materials through simultaneously incorporating two functional
groups into the 1,3-enyne systems with high levels of regio-,
chemo-, and stereocontol.
2−4
Significant methods are 1,3-
enyne alkylative 1,4-dicarbofunctionalization with alkyl halides
via cross coupling, such as 1,4-dialkylation, 1,4-alkylarylation,
and 1,4-diarylation, which allow incorporation of two
carbofunctional groups to the 1,3-enynes leading to complex
allenes (Scheme 1A).
3
These works are mainly focused on
transition-metal (often nickel) catalysis for the redox-neutral
1,3-enyne 1,4-dicarbofunctionalization with alkyl halides and
organometallics,
3a,d
reductive 1,3-enyne 1,4-dicarbofunctional-
ization with two electrophilic organohalides by cooperative
metal reducing reagents, electroreductive catalysis, and/or
photoreductive catalysis,
3e,h
thus giving rise to practical issues,
such as the high cost of the catalytic system and the need for
both prefunctionalized starting materials and limited terminat-
ing carbofunctional groups. Therefore, there is a need for
developing mechanistically distinct strategies that allow
incorporation of broad classes of readily accessible carbofunc-
tional group feedstocks in 1,3-enyne systems without
transition-metal catalysis to accomplish 1,3-enyne dicarbo-
functionalization and assemble diverse functionalized allenes
with high regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity.
Halogen atom transfer (XAT) is a fundamental elementary
strategy, which engages the transformations of organohalides
with nucleophilic XAT agents (such as traditional organotins,
silicon reagents, trialkylborane-O
2
systems, and current
alkylamines) into transposed carbon-centered radicals using
thermochemical, photochemical, or electrochemical catalysis,
in synthetic chemistry to fuel the mania for new reaction
creation.
5
Particularly, recent achievements in photocatalytic
methods employing alkylamines as XAT agents are effective for
allowing C−X (X = halogen) functionalization of organo-
halides via XAT.
5e,l
To our knowledge, however, there are no
reports documenting the successful use of XAT of organo-
halides to enable 1,4-difunctionalization of 1,3-enynes.

On this basis, we envisaged that using a tertiary amine as an
electron transfer agent drives XAT of organohalides to form
transposed carbon-centered radicals, which would implement
regioselective addition across the alkene moiety, subsequent
isomerization, and radical−radical coupling to realize 1,3-
enyne 4-difunctionalization. Herein, we report a new photo-
reductive 1,4-alkylarylation of 1,3-enynes with alkyl iodides
and cyanoarenes
6
via XAT for producing polysubstituted
allenes in a highly regio-, stereo-, and chemoselective manner
(Scheme 1B). Upon photoredox catalysis and activation of
tertiary alkyl amine XAT agents, this method enables the
formation of two C−C bonds, including a C(sp
3

through single electron oxidation (SEO) to generate the amine
radical cation, XAT, via radical addition across the C�C
bonds, single electron reduction (SER), radical−radical
coupling, and decyanation cascades, and provides a general
avenue to polysubstituted allenes, utilizing readily accessible
starting materials. Moreover, this strategy is applicable to 1,4-
diarylation of 1,3-enynes with aryl iodides and cyanoarenes.

more reactive than the electron-withdrawing ones. While
isonicotinonitriles having an electron-donating group like Me
or MeO furnished 38 and 39, respectively, in 60−61% yields,
the variant containing an electron-withdrawing F group
delivered 40 in a slightly diminished yield. The important
aryl and alkynyl functionalities can survive, assembling 41−44
in 50−65% yields. 2,6-DiMe-substituted isonicotinonitrile is a
suitable substrate and afforded 45 in 62% yield.
8
Unfortu-
nately, terephthalonitrile had no reactivity (46).
As shown in Scheme 2, we explored the feasibility of aryl
halides for this 1,3-enyne 1,4-difunctionalization protocol (eq
1). We found that iodobenzene was viable for constructing 47
in 52% yield, but bromobenzene and chlorobenzene were not
suitable substrates. Aryl iodides bearing a substituent, such as
MeO and acetyl, at the meta, ortho, or para positions, could be
converted to 48−50 in moderate to good yields. The control
experiments with a radical scavenger such as TEMPO, BHT,
BQ, and 1,1-diphenyalkene were examined. The reaction was
completely inhibited when using TEMPO, BQ, or 1,1-
diphenyalkene, providing the TEMPO-trapping product 51
(eq 2; Scheme 2). Using BHT also suppressed the reaction
with a sharply diminishing yield. These experiments support
the involvement of a radical process in this reaction.

Based on the current mechanistic studies and literature

Single electron oxidation (SEO) of Et

iodide 2a to afford the alkyl carbon-centered radical B.
5

new alkyl radical intermediate C. During the process, single
electron reduction (SER) of isonicotinonitrile 3a by the [Ir

anion intermediate D and regenerate the active [Ir
III

photocatalyst.
6
Finally, intermediate C undergoes radical−
radical coupling with intermediate D and subsequent
decyanation, accessing the desired allene.

alkyl iodides and cyanoarenes for forging polysubstituted
allenes in a highly regio-, chemo-, and stereoselective fashion.
